Routine Descriptions

THM_ASI_CAL_ADAPTER

 [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_cal_adapter

PURPOSE:
  Build a calibration structure from a skymap that is drop-in
  compatible with what thm_load_asi_cal returns from the legacy Berkeley
  thg_l2_asc v02 calibration CDFs: a cdf_load_vars-style structure with
  .vars[i].name / .vars[i].dataptr, containing the 40 variables of the
  v02 cal files in the exact same order (some consumers index vars by
  position, e.g. the /autocenter code in thm_asi_create_mosaic).

  Variable sources (skymap tag -> cal variable):
    full_azimuth/full_elevation (ORIENTed)      -> thg_asf_<site>_azim/_elev [256,256]
    full_map_longitude/latitude[*,*,i] (ORIENT) -> thg_asf_<site>_glon/_glat [257,257]
                                                   (all 3 altitude planes kept? no --
                                                    the 110 km plane, like v02 cal)
    full_map_altitude                           -> thg_asf_<site>_alti [3]
    full_ignore/full_subtract/full_multiply/full_bin (ORIENTed)
                                                -> _mask/_offset/_multiply/_bin
    bin_azimuth/bin_elevation                   -> thg_ast_<site>_azim/_elev [1024]
    bin_column/bin_row                          -> thg_ast_<site>_binc/_binr [1024]
    transpose(bin_map_longitude/latitude)       -> thg_ast_<site>_glon/_glat [4,1024]
                                                   (longitude converted to +-180,
                                                    matching the v02 cal convention)
    site_map_longitude/latitude/altitude        -> thg_asc_<site>_glon/_glat/_alti
    asf arrays at CCD column 127                -> thg_ask_<site>_* [256]
                                                   (same convention as the v02
                                                    mlat/mlon patch in thm_load_asi_cal)

  Magnetic coordinates (_mlat/_mlon) are filled with NaN: no SPEDAS ASI
  consumer uses them (verified), and the skymaps do not carry AACGM
  coordinates. thg_asc_<site>_midn (MLT midnight string) is likewise not
  derivable from the skymap and is set to ''.

INPUT:
  skymap:   restored skymap structure (from thm_asi_skymap)
  site:     4-letter site code (string)
  filename: skymap file path (recorded in the .filename tag)

OUTPUT:
  cal structure {filename, inq, compression, gzip_level, g_attributes,
                 g_att_names, nv, vars[40]}

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_cal_adapter.pro)

THM_ASI_CAL_ADAPTER_REGO

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_cal_adapter_rego

PURPOSE:
  Build a REGO calibration structure from a REGO skymap that is
  drop-in compatible with what thm_load_asi_cal,/rego returns from the
  legacy Berkeley rego_l2_asc v01 calibration CDFs: a cdf_load_vars-style
  structure with .vars[i].name / .vars[i].dataptr containing the 40
  variables in the exact legacy order (positions verified against the
  real rego_l2_asc_gill_19700101_v01.cdf; site-center scalars sit at
  vars[20]/vars[21] like the THEMIS files).

  Differences from the THEMIS adapter, per the legacy REGO cal layout:
    - 512x512 full-resolution arrays; corner grids are [3,513,513] with
      ALL THREE altitude planes (110/150/230 km), not a single plane
    - variable prefixes clg_rgf_ (full), clg_rgt_ (1024-bin thumb),
      clg_rgk_ (keogram), clg_asc_ (site scalars)
    - extra full-frame variables flat / c512 / c513

  Magnetic coordinates (_mlat/_mlon) and clg_asc_<site>_midn are filled
  with NaN/'' (the legacy files populate them, but no SPEDAS consumer
  reads them, and skymaps do not carry AACGM coordinates).

  Verified against rego_l2_asc_gill_19700101_v01.cdf: all 40 names and
  positions match, and azim/elev/glon/glat (all 3 altitude planes),
  mask/offset/flat/multiply/alti/c512/c513, the full rgt bin set, and the
  asc site scalars are numerically EXACT. Two documented deviations, both
  consumer-free (verified no SPEDAS code reads them):
    - clg_rgf_<site>_bin: legacy per-pixel bin-ID map differs slightly
      (mean ~11 of 1024; the bin geometry itself -- rgt binc/binr/corner
      maps -- is exact), likely an older generation pass in the legacy file
    - clg_rgk_<site>_*: the legacy keogram-cal arrays are only partially
      filled (202 of 512 entries, elevations near horizon only) and match
      no rgf slice; the adapter instead provides a clean center-meridian
      convention (CCD column 256 reversed / corner columns 256/255),
      analogous to the THEMIS ask cal

INPUT:
  skymap:   restored REGO skymap structure (thm_asi_skymap,/rego)
  site:     4-letter site code (string)
  filename: skymap file path (recorded in the .filename tag)

OUTPUT:
  cal structure {filename, inq, compression, gzip_level, g_attributes,
                 g_att_names, nv, vars[40]}

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_cal_adapter_rego.pro)

THM_ASI_CONFIG

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_config

PURPOSE:
  Central configuration for the THEMIS ASI and REGO data loading path.
  All dataset names, endpoints, and cache conventions used by the
  thm_asi_* routines live here so that product/dataset changes are
  one-line edits.

  The API base URL can be overridden with the THM_ASI_API_URL
  environment variable (useful for testing against staging servers).

OUTPUT:
  Structure of configuration constants.

NOTES:
  Data documentation: https://data.phys.ucalgary.ca
  API documentation:  https://api.phys.ucalgary.ca

  Data files are cached under !themis.local_data_dir + 'thg/asi/' +
  <DATASET_NAME>, mirroring the archive tree below each dataset's
  data_tree_url. Caches from before the 2026-08 rename (thg/ucalgary/)
  are migrated automatically on first use.

THM_ASI_DEDUP_GZ

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_dedup_gz

PURPOSE:
  Some archive trees (notably the stream2 keogram products)
  contain BOTH an uncompressed file and its gzipped twin (e.g.
  ..._full-keogram.pgm and ..._full-keogram.pgm.gz), and the data
  distribution API lists both. Downloading/reading both wastes transfer
  and duplicates every data record. This function reduces a list of URLs
  or file paths to one entry per logical file, PREFERRING the .gz
  variant; entries that only exist uncompressed (it happens: e.g. atha
  2008-02-10 ut14 hourly keogram) are kept as-is.

INPUT:
  files: string array of URLs or paths

OUTPUT:
  Filtered string array (original order preserved).

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_dedup_gz.pro)

THM_ASI_DOWNLOAD

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_download

PURPOSE:
  Download THEMIS ASI and REGO data files from the data archive
  (data.phys.ucalgary.ca) for a given dataset, timeframe, and optional
  site. File URLs are resolved with thm_asi_get_urls (the
  api.phys.ucalgary.ca data distribution endpoint) and fetched with the
  standard SPEDAS spd_download, so proxy/network behavior matches the
  rest of SPEDAS.

  Files are cached under
    !themis.local_data_dir + 'thg/asi/<DATASET_NAME>/<archive tree>'
  mirroring the archive layout below the dataset's data_tree_url
  (the same convention idl-aurorax uses, but rooted in the SPEDAS data
  directory). Files already present in the cache are not re-downloaded
  (the archive files are immutable).

INPUT:
  dataset_name: dataset to download, e.g. 'THEMIS_ASI_RAW' (string)
  start_ts:     start timestamp, ISO format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (string)
  end_ts:       end timestamp (inclusive), same format (string)

KEYWORDS:
  site_uid:    4-letter site UID filter, e.g. 'fykn' (string)
  device_uid:  device UID filter, e.g. 'themis08' (string)
  no_download: if set, do not contact the API or server at all; returns
               count=0 (callers fall back to globbing the local cache)
  verbose:     dprint verbosity passthrough

OUTPUT:
  Structure:
    { files:     string array of local absolute paths (only files that
                 exist locally after the call),
      count:     number of elements in files,
      relpaths:  archive-tree-relative paths (below data_tree_url),
      data_tree_url: the dataset's archive root URL,
      total_urls: number of URLs the API listed,
      api_ok:    1b if the API responded (even with zero URLs), 0b if the
                 API was not contacted or the request failed }
  Returns count=0 structure if nothing was listed/downloaded.

EXAMPLE:
  d = thm_asi_download('THEMIS_ASI_RAW', $
        '2008-02-10T07:00:00','2008-02-10T07:59:59', site_uid='fykn')

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_download.pro)

THM_ASI_FILES_IN_WINDOW

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_files_in_window

PURPOSE:
  Filter a list of archive file paths to those whose filename start
  timestamp lies within [t0, t1] -- the same "file START time in
  [start, end]" rule the data distribution API applies to listings, so
  the offline cache-glob fallbacks resolve the same file set the server
  query would.

  Without this, the hour/day globs can catch granules far outside the
  request window: a single-frame time= request globs every minute file
  of the hour (~60x the data needed), and an ast/VEC1024 time= request
  globs every hourly file of the day.

  Archive basenames start 'YYYYMMDD_hhmm_' (minute granules) or
  'YYYYMMDD_hh_' (hour granules); files whose basename does not match
  either form are kept (fail open).

INPUT:
  files:  string array of file paths
  t0, t1: window bounds (unix time, inclusive)

KEYWORDS:
  count: (out) number of files kept

OUTPUT:
  Filtered string array ('' when count is 0; original order preserved).

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_files_in_window.pro)

THM_ASI_GET_URLS

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_get_urls

PURPOSE:
  Retrieve the URLs of files available for download from the data
  archive for a given dataset, timeframe, and optional site.
  This is the file-listing step of this loading path for
  THEMIS ASI data; the file GETs themselves are done by
  thm_asi_download.

INPUT:
  dataset_name: dataset to list, e.g. 'THEMIS_ASI_RAW' (string)
  start_ts:     start timestamp, ISO format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (string)
  end_ts:       end timestamp (inclusive), same format (string)

KEYWORDS:
  site_uid:   4-letter site UID to filter on, e.g. 'fykn' (string)
  device_uid: device UID to filter on, e.g. 'themis08' (string)
  verbose:    dprint verbosity passthrough

OUTPUT:
  Structure with tags urls (list of full https URLs), count, path_prefix,
  and dataset (struct with data_tree_url etc.), as returned by the API.
  Returns !null on any request/parse failure.

EXAMPLE:
  u = thm_asi_get_urls('THEMIS_ASI_RAW', $
        '2008-02-10T07:00:00','2008-02-10T07:59:59', site_uid='fykn')

NOTES:
  Proxies are resolved by thm_asi_proxy, so a proxy configured the
  usual SPEDAS way works here with no extra setup:
    setenv, 'http_proxy=http://proxy.example.org:3128'

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_get_urls.pro)

THM_ASI_LOAD_ASK

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  thm_asi_load_ask

PURPOSE:
  Load THEMIS ASI or REGO keograms ('ask') from the data archive
  (data.phys.ucalgary.ca) into tplot variables compatible with the legacy Berkeley ask
  CDF loader output:
    thg_ask_<site>: {x: double[n], y: uint[n,256], v: [256]}  (spec=1)
    clg_ask_<site>: {x: double[n], y: uint[n,512], v: [512]}  (/rego)

  THEMIS: hourly keogram PGMs (THEMIS_ASI_HOURLY_KEOGRAM_PGM) are
  stitched across the requested range -- 600 columns/hour = one column
  per 6 s vs one per 3-s frame in the legacy CDFs (visually equivalent,
  corr 0.98-0.99 at matched times, not byte-identical). Use the default
  Berkeley CDF path of thm_load_ask (omit /ucalgary_pgm) if exact legacy
  values are required.

  REGO (/rego): hourly keograms are 1200 columns/hour = the full 3-s
  cadence, read from the 16-bit grayscale PNG product
  (REGO_HOURLY_KEOGRAM_PNG), which covers the whole mission -- the PGM
  twin only exists from ~Oct 2016 and is bit-identical where both exist.

  IMPORTANT -- REGO keogram values are NOT counts. Unlike the THEMIS
  keogram products, which are plain counts, the REGO ones are display-
  scaled by the onsite generator: a fixed count window is mapped linearly
  onto 0-65535 and everything outside it is clipped, so faint pixels
  bottom out at 0 and bright aurora saturates at 65535. Structure and
  timing are correct -- the keograms plot correctly -- but the values are
  not photometric and must not be used as intensities. This is flagged in
  the variable's units ('scaled_counts', in both data_att and the CDF
  vatt), in the color-bar title set by thm_load_ask, and by a dprint at
  load time. Use the default Berkeley CDF path of thm_load_ask (omit
  /ucalgary_pgm) for count-accurate keograms, or load the raw images with
  thm_load_rego to apply a scaling of your own.

  The same scaling is used throughout the REGO dataset -- every site,
  every date -- so keograms are directly comparable across stations and
  nights and there is no per-file scale factor to track. Characterised
  empirically against REGO_RAW, the map is
    archived = round((counts - 280) * 65535/1030.7), clipped to 0-65535
  which is one-to-one inside the window. It is deliberately not inverted
  here: the clipped tails are unrecoverable either way, and the default
  Berkeley CDF path is the supported path to counts.

  Empirical alignment vs the legacy CDFs: PGM rows are stored opposite
  to the legacy orientation (reverse the 2nd dimension) while the REGO
  PNGs are already legacy-ordered; column j represents the frame at
  hour_start + j*binw (zero offset).

  Internal worker for thm_load_ask; users should keep calling thm_load_ask.

KEYWORDS:
  sites:        string array of 4-letter site codes (lowercase)
  trange:       time range (defaults to timerange()); output IS clipped
                to trange, like the legacy ask loader
  suffix:       appended to tplot variable names
  rego:         load REGO keograms (clg_ask_*) instead of THEMIS ASI
  downloadonly: download files but do not load into tplot
  no_download:  do not contact server; use only the local cache
  verbose:      dprint verbosity
  files:        (in/out) accumulates local file paths across the sites in
                this call. NOTE the public loader (thm_load_ask) collects
                these in a local and ASSIGNS its own files keyword once, so
                that repeated calls replace rather than grow the caller's
                variable -- the legacy thm_load_xxx contract, which the
                SPEDAS GUI relies on (it reuses one variable per load).
  relpathnames_all: (in/out) accumulates cache-relative paths, same contract
  tplotnames:   (out) accumulates created tplot variable names

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_load_ask.pro)

THM_ASI_LOAD_IMG

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  thm_asi_load_img

PURPOSE:
  Load THEMIS ASI image data (full-resolution 'asf' or thumbnail 'ast')
  from the data archive at data.phys.ucalgary.ca into tplot variables that are
  drop-in compatible with the legacy Berkeley CDF loader output:
    thg_asf_<site>: {x: double[n], y: uint[n,256,256], v1:[256], v2:[256]}
    thg_ast_<site>: {x: double[n], y: uint[n,32,32],  v1:[32],  v2:[32]}
  with matching dlimits (cdf/gatt/vatt shape, spec=0, units 'counts').

  This is an internal worker for thm_load_asi; users should keep calling
  thm_load_asi.

KEYWORDS:
  sites:        string array of 4-letter site codes (lowercase)
  datatype:     'asf' or 'ast' (scalar)
  trange:       time range (defaults to timerange()); whole file granules
                are fetched (1-min files for asf/rgf, hourly files for
                ast) and the output is clipped to trange unless
                /no_time_clip is set
  no_time_clip: store every frame of every fetched file instead of
                clipping the output to trange (output then aligns to
                file-granule boundaries)
  time:         load only the single frame nearest this time (+-1.5 s);
                output y is 2-D, matching the legacy single-record read
  suffix:       appended to tplot variable names
  downloadonly: download files but do not load into tplot
  no_download:  do not contact server; use only the local cache
  verbose:      dprint verbosity
  files:        (in/out) accumulates local file paths across the sites in
                this call. NOTE the public loaders (thm_load_asi /
                thm_load_rego) collect these in a local and ASSIGN their own
                files keyword once, so that repeated calls replace rather
                than grow the caller's variable -- the legacy thm_load_xxx
                contract, which the SPEDAS GUI relies on (it reuses one
                variable per load).
  relpathnames_all: (in/out) accumulates cache-relative paths, same contract
  tplotnames:   (out) accumulates created tplot variable names

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_load_img.pro)

THM_ASI_ORIENT

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_orient

PURPOSE:
  Apply the single authoritative orientation transform that maps a raw
  archive image array (as returned by thm_asi_readfile,
  in native PGM orientation) onto the orientation used by the legacy
  Berkeley THEMIS ASI CDF images (thg_asf_<site> / thg_ast_<site>).

  The transform is rotate(img, 2), i.e. a 180-degree rotation. It was
  pinned empirically (2026-08-07) by comparing all 20 frames of
  20080210_0713_fykn_themis14_full.pgm.gz against the same frames in
  thg_l1_asf_fykn_2008021007_v01.cdf: rotate(...,2) reproduces the CDF
  pixel values bit-identically; all other rotate() directions match
  zero frames.

  The same transform must be applied to any per-pixel calibration arrays
  derived from skymaps (elevation, azimuth, corner grids) so
  that they stay aligned with the images. For the 257x257 corner grids
  the 180-degree rotation maps corner (i,j) -> (256-i,256-j), which
  rotate(...,2) also handles correctly.

INPUT:
  img: 2-D image or calibration array (any type)

OUTPUT:
  the array rotated 180 degrees

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_orient.pro)

THM_ASI_PROXY

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_proxy

PURPOSE:
  Resolve the HTTP proxy configuration to use for THEMIS ASI / REGO
  archive traffic, returned with IDLnetURL property names so the result
  can be applied directly with IDLnetURL::SetProperty or handed to
  spd_download through _extra.

  This exists so that the API listing call (thm_asi_get_urls,
  which drives its own IDLnetURL object) obeys the same proxy settings as
  the file downloads, which go through spd_download and therefore already
  pick up http_proxy inside spd_download_file.

  Resolution order:
    1. AURORAX_PROXY_HOSTNAME and AURORAX_PROXY_PORT (with optional
       AURORAX_PROXY_USERNAME / AURORAX_PROXY_PASSWORD). This is the
       idl-aurorax convention, kept so existing setups keep working, and
       treated as an override because it is the more specific setting.
    2. http_proxy, the standard SPEDAS convention, parsed by spd_get_proxy
       -- the exact call spd_download_file makes -- so a proxy configured
       the usual SPEDAS way needs no extra setup here:
         setenv, 'http_proxy=http://user:pass@proxy.example.org:3128'

KEYWORDS:
  verbose: dprint verbosity passthrough

OUTPUT:
  Structure with proxy_hostname, proxy_port, proxy_username and
  proxy_password tags, or !null when no proxy is configured. Passing an
  undefined/!null value through _extra is a no-op in IDL, so callers can
  forward the result unconditionally.

NOTES:
  spd_get_proxy leaves its argument undefined when http_proxy is unset or
  unparseable, which is what makes the !null return work.

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_proxy.pro)

THM_ASI_READFILE[3]

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  thm_asi_readfile

PURPOSE:
  Read one or more archive PGM / PGM.GZ files (multi-frame
  one-minute raw bundles, hourly thumb32 bundles, or daily keogram files)
  into a frame stack plus per-frame metadata.

INPUT:
  filename: string or string array of files to read (sorted internally)

OUTPUT:
  images:   [width, height, n_frames] byte or uint array (per PGM maxval)
  metadata: n_frames-element array of thm_asi_Pgm_Metadata

KEYWORDS:
  count:       returns number of frames read
  no_metadata: skip comment parsing (metadata contains defaults)
  minimal_metadata: only parse timestamps
  first_frame: stop after the first frame of each file
  verbose:     dprint verbosity

NOTES:
  Frames are returned in raw PGM orientation; callers must apply
  thm_asi_orient to match the orientation of the legacy
  Berkeley CDF images.

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_readfile.pro)

THM_ASI_SKYMAP

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_skymap

PURPOSE:
  Locate, download, and restore the best skymap for a THEMIS ASI
  site at a given time: the skymap with the latest validity start time at
  or before the requested time. If the requested time predates
  all available skymaps, the earliest one is used with a warning.

INPUT:
  site: 4-letter site code, e.g. 'fykn' (string)
  time: requested time (double unix time or string)

KEYWORDS:
  no_download: use only the local cache
  verbose:     dprint verbosity
  filename:    (out) local path of the restored skymap file
  rego:        use the REGO skymap dataset instead of THEMIS ASI

OUTPUT:
  the restored skymap structure, or -1 if none could be obtained

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_skymap.pro)

THM_ASI_TIME

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_time

PURPOSE:
  Convert per-frame metadata from thm_asi_readfile into unix
  times (double, seconds since 1970-01-01 with no leap seconds) -- the
  same time convention used by the legacy Berkeley THEMIS ASI CDFs.

INPUT:
  metadata: array of thm_asi_Pgm_Metadata structures

OUTPUT:
  double array of unix times (one per frame)

NOTES:
  The exposure start strings are 'YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss[.ssssss]' UTC,
  which time_double parses directly.

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_time.pro)

THM_ASI_USE_ARCHIVE

 [Previous Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  thm_asi_use_archive

PURPOSE:
  Single place that decides which loading path the THEMIS ASI / REGO
  loaders (thm_load_asi, thm_load_rego, thm_load_ask, thm_load_asi_cal)
  and the mosaic routines take for a given pair of keywords:

    /CDF_LEGACY   -> Berkeley CDF path (always wins when set)
    /UCALGARY_PGM  -> data archive path (data.phys.ucalgary.ca)
    neither       -> the DEFAULT, currently the Berkeley CDF path

  To make the data archive the default instead, change only the last
  line of this function to
      return, 1b
  Every caller passes both keywords through, so no other file needs to
  change for the flip, and /cdf_legacy keeps working as the way back.

INPUT KEYWORDS:
  ucalgary_pgm: request the data archive path
  cdf_legacy:  request the Berkeley CDF path

OUTPUT:
  1b if the data archive path should be used, 0b for the Berkeley CDF path

(See projects/themis/ground/asi/thm_asi_use_archive.pro)
